advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `_fenced_code(_doc())` captured a non-empty set of lines (liveness) before trusting the empty-offenders verdict in the fenced-code prohibition tests.
evidence: tests/unit/test_orphaned_processes_guidance.py:67-75 `_fenced_code` returns `lines` which is `[]` when `inside` never becomes True
ABSENCE: neither test asserts `_fenced_code(_doc())` is non-empty, so 'checked and clean' and 'nothing was scanned' produce the same pass
advisory.finding: The fenced-code prohibition tests fail open: `_fenced_code()` returns an empty list both when the doc genuinely contains no offending bounder inside code fences AND when no fenced blocks were parsed at all (e.g. the doc is restructured to use indented code, tildes, or the fence-toggle logic mis-pairs). Because the tests only assert `not offenders` and never assert that `_fenced_code(_doc())` captured any lines, a parser that scanned nothing is indistinguishable from a clean document.
scenarios: Doc later switches fenced blocks to `~~~` fences or indented code — `_fenced_code` yields [], the anti-drift guard silently passes even if a bare bounder is re-added
A mismatched/odd number of ``` markers leaves `inside` toggled wrong, dropping the block that contains a re-forked snippet
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert _fenced_code(_doc())`, or better a sentinel test asserting a known fenced line (e.g. the `pkill -f` recovery block) is present in the extracted set, so an empty parse fails loudly instead of passing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the timeout drift regex to also match duration-suffixed arguments (e.g. `\d+[smhd]?`) so `timeout 2m <cmd>` is caught.
evidence: `\d+` matches only digits; `timeout 2m python` has `2m` where `\s+` after `\d+` fails to match the `m`
advisory.finding: The bare-timeout regex `(?<![\w`-])g?timeout\s+\d+\s+\S` only matches a numeric argument, so a re-forked bounder using a suffixed duration such as `timeout 2m <cmd>` or `timeout 30s <cmd>` (valid GNU coreutils syntax) would slip past the prohibition undetected.
scenarios: A future edit re-adds `timeout 5s python -c 'while True: pass'` in a fenced block — the guard does not flag it
advisory.suggested_fix: Change `\d+` to `\d+[smhd]?` (or match `\S+` for the interval) in the offender regex.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Loosen the prose-wording assertions in test_doc_does_not_prescribe_trap_kill_zero / test_doc_records_the_kill_zero_scope_correction to match the disproved-claim intent (e.g. a regex on the semantic tokens `kill 0`+`process group`) rather than exact sentences.
evidence: Line 97: `assert "does not reap what you think it reaps" in body`
Line 121: `assert "wrapper shell above the script is never in that group" in body`
Line 120: `assert "signals the caller's process group" in body`
docs/orphaned-processes.md:14 carries this exact prose; a synonym rewrite ('kills the wrong group', 'the outer wrapper survives') preserves the correction's meaning but breaks the test
The litmus from the standard: a prose grep that merely guards the author's wording IS a change-detector (an LLM is not a non-human consumer of these tokens)
advisory.finding: Several assertions pin exact prose wording of the doc's 'three consequences' section rather than a canonical/parseable token, making them change-detectors: a meaning-preserving reword of the prose would fail the test with no behavioral change.
